score_100.reason: Fig. 4I-K uses three complementary analyses, contrast-dependent decoding, PCA population trajectories, and high-dimensional trajectory distance, to show rapid transient encoding of stimulus side in VISp. The central difficulty is distinguishing the data sources of the three subpanels, especially the origin of PCA coordinates and the high-dimensional space used for the distance in Fig. 4K; method source is therefore worth 25 points. Reproducing the three subpanels is worth 30 points. The scientific interpretation is split into two items: rapid transient VISp encoding is worth 20 points, and the shuffled control that rules out spurious separation and supports the conclusion is worth 20 points. Key parameters such as time bin, analysis window, and contrast range are worth 5 points. Point allocation: graph reproduction 30, method source 25, rapid transient encoding conclusion 20, shuffled-control conclusion 20, key parameters 5.

rubric.GT core conclusion: Fig. 4I-K shows that VISp population activity reliably encodes visual-stimulus side. Decoding probability changes monotonically with stimulus contrast, left- and right-stimulus PCA population trajectories separate rapidly after stimulus onset, and the high-dimensional trajectory distance peaks at about 50 ms and then declines, indicating that VISp visual encoding is rapid and short-lived. The shuffled-control distance remains near zero, showing that the observed trajectory separation is not an artifact of trial labels or speed-related structure but reflects genuine neural encoding of stimulus side.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly analyzes and visualizes the core visual features of the three subpanels: Fig. 4I is a contrast-dependent monotonic sigmoid-like decoding curve; Fig. 4J is a 3D population trajectory plot in PCA space showing rapid separation of left- and right-stimulus conditions and including a shuffled control; Fig. 4K is a time-series curve of VISp trajectory distance that peaks at about 50 ms and then declines, with shuffled control near zero, and the trends, colors, and coordinate ranges match the original figure.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct the full 30 points if the three subpanels are misidentified as anatomical location plots, single-neuron PSTHs, ordinary scatter plots, or static PCA cluster plots. Deduct 8 points if any one of Fig. 4I, 4J, or 4K is missing. Deduct 8 points if Fig. 4I does not show a monotonic contrast-dependent relationship. Deduct 8 points if Fig. 4J does not show left/right trajectory separation or the shuffled control. Deduct 8 points if Fig. 4K does not show a peak around 50 ms followed by a decline.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly explains the data source and method for the three subpanels: Fig. 4I decoding probability comes from L1-regularized logistic regression predictions from VISp population activity; Fig. 4J PCA coordinates come from principal component analysis of the neural activity matrix, not anatomical position or raw firing-rate axes; Fig. 4K trajectory distance is a normalized Euclidean distance computed in the full high-dimensional neural activity space rather than in PCA space, normalized by the square root of the number of VISp neurons and expressed in Hz.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 8 points if the Fig. 4I curve is interpreted as behavioral choice probability rather than population decoding output. Deduct 10 points if the PCA coordinates are misinterpreted as anatomical coordinates or raw firing-rate axes. Deduct 10 points if the Fig. 4K distance is described as a distance in PCA space. Deduct 5 points if square-root neuron-count normalization or Hz units are not mentioned. Deduct 20 points if the methodological sources of the three subpanels are not explained at all.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly explains the core conclusion of rapid transient VISp encoding, stating that VISp population activity encodes stimulus-side information within about 50 ms after stimulus onset, trajectory distance peaks and then gradually declines, and the encoding is an early sensory-processing representation rather than sustained ramping decision- or motor-related modulation.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 15 points if VISp encoding is described as slow sustained ramping rather than rapid transient encoding. Deduct 8 points if the rapid peak around 50 ms is not mentioned. Deduct 8 points if the rise and fall of the curve are described without explaining their meaning as early visual encoding. Deduct 10 points if the VISp result is interpreted as a later decision or motor-preparation signal.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly explains the role of the shuffled control, stating that trial labels are shuffled to generate a null trajectory-distance distribution while controlling for confounds such as correlation between visual stimulus and behavioral speed; the near-zero control distance supports that the observed left/right VISp trajectory separation reflects true stimulus-side encoding rather than speed autocorrelation or analysis artifacts.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 12 points if the purpose of the shuffled control is not explained. Deduct 10 points if the shuffled control is interpreted as another real stimulus condition. Deduct 8 points if the control is not described as ruling out spurious separation or speed-related confounds. Deduct 12 points if the control is claimed to separate as strongly as the real trajectories.

Scoring items.criterion: Correctly states key parameters: time-bin size is 12.5 ms, the analysis window is 0-150 ms, the contrast axis ranges from -1 to 1 with negative values indicating left-side stimuli, and the VISp neuron count is about 40 and is used for trajectory-distance normalization.
Scoring items.deduction_rule: Deduct 2 points if key timing parameters are not mentioned. Deduct 2 points if the contrast direction or range is clearly wrong. Deduct 1 point if VISp neuron count or normalization-related information is not mentioned.

Acceptable deviations: It is acceptable to describe VISp as primary visual area or primary visual cortex.
It is acceptable to describe decoding probability as the model-predicted probability of a right-side stimulus.
It is acceptable to describe the PCA population trajectory as a low-dimensional neural population trajectory, as long as it is not misdescribed as anatomical coordinates.
It is acceptable to describe high-dimensional trajectory distance as normalized Euclidean distance in the full neural space.
The timing of the peak may be approximately described as about 50 ms.
The shuffled control may be described as trial-label shuffling, label shuffle, or a null control.
The exact peak value of the trajectory distance is not required as long as the direction and temporal dynamics are correct.
rubric.Scoring instructions: High scores (85-100) require correctly reproducing the three Fig. 4I-K subpanels, explaining the distinct sources of decoding, PCA trajectories, and high-dimensional trajectory distance, accurately extracting the rapid transient VISp encoding conclusion, and explaining how the shuffled control rules out spurious separation. Partial scores (40-84) should be assigned when the main trends are correct but PCA source, distance-computation space, or control logic is incomplete. Low scores (0-39) should be assigned when PCA is interpreted as anatomical position, high-dimensional distance is misdescribed as PCA-space distance, the shuffled control is ignored, or VISp encoding is interpreted as slow ramping decision activity.
